proposed.sourceName: Islam Q&A — Fatwa 2841 'Is Animal Rennet Halal?'
proposed.paraphrase: Presents the two scholarly positions on rennet from an animal not slaughtered Islamically: the majority (Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali) hold it najis (impure) and haram on the basis of the prohibition of carrion, while the minority (Abu Hanifa and one narration from Imam Ahmad, favored by Ibn Taymiyyah) hold it tahir (pure) because the enzyme does not die with the animal; it concludes the layperson must follow a qualified scholar on either view.

proposed.sourceName: Fiqh IslamOnline — 'Islamic Ruling on Parmesan Cheese'
proposed.paraphrase: States that microbial, vegetable, or non-animal rennet cheese is halal by consensus; for animal rennet from a non-Islamically-slaughtered animal it reports the Shafi'i/Maliki/Hanbali view that it is impure and forbidden versus the Hanafi view that the rennet is pure regardless of slaughter and therefore permissible.

researcherNote: enzyme/animal seeded zabiha grade 5 (Haram). The strict zabiha follower follows the majority (Maliki/Shafi'i/Hanbali) that rennet from a non-zabiha animal is najis/carrion and haram. Two independent tier-1 sources on the strict side. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01 (batch pre-approval).
